title: Year-over-Year Revenue Growth Using LAG
description:
Calculate year-over-year revenue growth amount and percentage for each year using the LAG window function.

**Table: annual_revenue** — `year`, `revenue`

Output columns: `year`, `revenue`, `prev_year_revenue`, `yoy_change`, `yoy_growth_pct`. Order by `year`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE annual_revenue (year INT, revenue DECIMAL(12,2)); INSERT INTO annual_revenue VALUES (2022,1200000.00),(2023,1450000.00),(2024,1380000.00),(2025,1620000.00),(2026,1890000.00);
solution_sql: SELECT year, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS prev_year_revenue, revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS yoy_change, ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year)) / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year), 2) AS yoy_growth_pct FROM annual_revenue ORDER BY year

test_cases.description: 5 years; 2022 has NULL for all prior-year columns; 2023-2026 have computed growth metrics

hints: LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year) fetches the previous year's revenue; the 2022 row (first year) returns NULL.
yoy_growth_pct = 100 * (current - previous) / previous; a negative value means revenue declined year over year.
explanation: LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year) looks back one row in chronological order. 2022: no prior year → NULL. 2023: 1450000-1200000=+250000, +20.83%. 2024: 1380000-1450000=-70000, -4.83% (decline). 2025: +240000, +17.39%. 2026: +270000, +16.67%. All 5 rows are returned with NULL metrics for the base year.
